quotes.maya: I dumped a messy iPhone rehearsal into it and got a chart I could actually play. Tweaked two bars, printed, made soundcheck. That would've been an hour of guesswork otherwise.
quotes.daniel: Cuts my prep in half. I export to MusicXML, add stickings for the kids, and hand out PDFs. Fewer "where do I come in?" moments, more time actually playing.
quotes.leo: Night-before gig. Four songs. It mapped the forms right, so rehearsal wasn't us arguing the bridge. We just ran it and locked to the click.
quotes.sofia: Slowed the tempo map, looped the chorus, finally nailed that triplet fill. Seeing the notes where I always rush was weirdly helpful.
quotes.chris: Clients show up with a reference track and ten minutes later the drummer has parts. No more "one more listen" meetings. We just hit record.
quotes.nora: Spacing is readable and the kit names aren't cryptic. I throw the PDF on the projector and the whole class follows the repeats without me yelling counts.
quotes.yuki: Batch three MP3s, download PDFs, drop into Premiere. That shaved a whole step off my tutorial workflow.
quotes.rahman: Fast queue matters when sessions stack. Drummers spend less time decoding and more time playing to the click. Simple win.
quotes.k: First charts I could follow end to end. Learned three songs this week without pausing YouTube every five seconds.

signup.q: How do I sign up/sign in?
signup.a: Use the Sign up / Sign in button in the top-right to create an account or sign in with SSO. After signing in you can access paid features from your account page.

split.q: How do I split a full track?
split.a: Upload the full track and use the split controls in the editor to choose segments. You can then process each segment separately.

expiration.q: What is the expiration date on paid packages?
expiration.a: Paid packages expire 12 months from the purchase date unless otherwise specified in the package details.

minutesMean.q: What does the "number of minutes in a pack" mean?
minutesMean.a: The minutes indicate the total processing audio time included in the pack; longer tracks use more minutes proportionally.

deducted.q: How are the minutes deducted from my account?
deducted.a: Minutes are deducted based on the length of audio you process. Partial minutes round up to the nearest second as described in billing.

remaining.q: Where can I see the number of remaining minutes?
remaining.a: Your remaining minutes are shown on your account dashboard under 'Billing & Usage'.

jobFails.q: What happens if a job fails?
jobFails.a: If a job fails we'll retry automatically; if it still fails we won't deduct minutes and you'll see a failure notice with options to retry or contact support.

addMinutes.q: How can I add more minutes to my account?
addMinutes.a: Visit the Pricing page and select an add-on pack or upgrade to a higher plan to increase your minutes.

quality.q: How do I improve the notation quality?
quality.a: Use higher-quality recordings, reduce background noise, and provide clear instrument separation for best results.

live.q: Will it work on live recordings?
live.a: Live recordings may work but results vary; studio-quality or clean recordings produce the best notation.

meters.q: Does it handle odd meters and tempo changes?
meters.a: Yes — the system detects tempo changes and odd meters, but accuracy improves with clear rhythmic content.

format.q: In what format will I receive the results?
format.a: You can download results as PDF, MusicXML, and MIDI depending on your plan.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: Does it work for my instrument?
faq.a1: Drums and piano today. Studio recordings give the cleanest notation; live phone recordings work but results vary. For other instruments you can separate the stems.
faq.a2: MP3, WAV, FLAC and OGG, up to 32 MB per file.
faq.q3: What happens when the {minutes} minutes run out?
faq.a3: Nothing. No charge, no expiring account. You stay on the free tier with 10-second previews, and you can top up whenever you want.
faq.a4: Yes: every result downloads as PDF, MusicXML and MIDI, so MuseScore, Sibelius and any DAW will open it.

signin.q: How do I sign up or sign in?
signin.a: Hit Sign In on the top right and pick Email, Google, Apple, or Facebook. We create your account on first sign-in, so there is no separate sign-up step.

stems.q: How do I split a track into stems?
stems.a: Upload your file, then choose Stem Splitter in the workspace. We separate drums, bass, piano, and vocals so you can process each segment on its own.

profile.q: How do I edit my profile?
profile.a: Open the account menu in the top right and choose Profile. You can change your display name, avatar, and email there.

connected.q: How do I manage connected accounts?
connected.a: Under Account → Connected accounts you can link or unlink Google, Apple, and Facebook. Keep at least one sign-in method connected.

delete.q: How do I delete my account?
delete.a: Account → Delete account. This permanently removes your uploads, scores, and minute balance. It cannot be undone.

minute.a: One billed minute equals one minute of your source track length, rounded up, regardless of how many instruments you export from it.

deducted.a: Minutes come off your balance only when a job completes successfully. Jobs that fail cost nothing.

expire.a: Monthly plan minutes reset each billing cycle and do not roll over. One-time top-up minutes never expire.

failed.q: What happens if a job fails?
failed.a: You are not charged any minutes. Retry from your history; re-encoding the source file usually fixes it.

add.q: How do I add more minutes?
add.a: Buy a one-time top-up from the Pricing page, or upgrade your plan for a higher monthly allowance.

refund.a: Refunds follow our Refund Policy, which sets out when a refund or credit is given. Contact us if you think you were charged in error.

plan.q: How do I change or cancel my plan?
plan.a: Account → Billing → Manage plan. Changes apply on your next cycle; cancel anytime and keep access until the period ends.

size.q: What is the maximum file size?

formats.q: Which audio formats can I upload?
formats.a: MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG and M4A.

outputs.q: What output formats do I get?
outputs.a: Every completed transcription gives you PDF, MusicXML, and MIDI.

clean.q: How do I get the cleanest notation?
clean.a: Use studio-quality recordings, isolate the instrument where you can, and pick the right kit mapping before processing.

live.a: They can, but results vary. Studio-quality recordings produce the best notation.

meters.q: Can it handle odd meters or tempo changes?
meters.a: Yes. We detect tempo maps and time signatures, including odd meters, though very fluid rubato is harder to track.

which.q: Which output format should I use?
which.a: MusicXML for editing in notation software, MIDI for DAWs, and PDF for reading or printing.

publish.q: How do I publish a score?
publish.a: Open a finished score and hit Publish to share it on Explore.

visibility.q: What do the visibility options mean?
visibility.a: Public appears on Explore and in search. Unlisted is reachable by link only. Private is visible to just you.

downloads.q: Who can download my published score?
downloads.a: You choose: allow downloads for everyone, for signed-in users only, or for no one.

unpublish.a: Open the score → Publishing → Unpublish. It is removed from Explore immediately.

creator.q: What shows on my creator profile?
creator.a: Your public scores (and unlisted ones opened via link), your display name, and your avatar.

pricingPage.title: Simple, minute-based pricing for working musicians.
pricingPage.subhead: 1 minute of audio = 1 minute of credit. Start free, upgrade for higher limits and advanced features. No surprises.
pricingPage.productDescription: Minute-based credit for AI music transcription, stem separation and audio-to-MIDI. Preview free, pay only for the audio you process.

trust.formats: All formats included: PDF · MusicXML · MIDI

minute.q: What does a minute of credit mean?
minute.a: 1 minute of audio = 1 minute of credit. A 3-minute song uses 3 minutes, the same whichever instrument you transcribe and whatever format you export.

deduct.q: How are minutes deducted from my account?
deduct.a: Minutes are deducted from the length of audio you process, rounded up to the nearest second. You can see your remaining balance any time under Billing & Usage in your account.

expire.a: Plan minutes refresh at the start of each billing cycle and don’t roll over. Top-up minutes never expire. They stay on your account until you use them.

fail.q: What happens if a job fails?
fail.a: We retry automatically. If it still fails we don’t deduct any minutes, and you’ll see a failure notice with options to retry or contact support.

add.q: How do I add more minutes?
add.a: Buy a one-time top-up from the Top-Ups tab above, or upgrade your plan for a higher monthly allowance. Top-ups apply instantly.

refund.a: Unused top-up minutes may be eligible for a refund. See our Refund Policy for the full details and how to request one.

change.q: How do I change or cancel my plan?
change.a: Manage, upgrade, downgrade or cancel anytime from the Stripe billing portal in your account settings. Changes take effect on your next billing date.

v1_9.title: WeChat Pay, and a smoother road to the full song

items.wechat: Top-ups priced in yuan can now be paid with WeChat Pay as well as by card. Subscriptions are still card only.
items.keepPreview: Your preview now waits for you while you sign in and pay. Pick a minute pack, sign in, check out, and the full song starts on its own.
items.phones: Song pages, Explore and search work better on phones: the song title sits above the player, the controls fit on one row and the tabs scroll.
items.signIn: Signing in from mainland China puts email first, and the code screen tells you where the code went and to check your spam folder.
items.downloads: Fixed: finished previews no longer start downloads on their own, and a dropped file is no longer uploaded twice.

v1_8.title: A page for every part, and more of the site in Chinese

items.partPages: Every transcribed part now has its own page, such as a song's drum score or its piano score, listing the downloads that part actually has.
items.chinese: Song pages, Help, Pricing, Explore and the stem splitter and MIDI converter pages are now in Simplified and Traditional Chinese.
items.previewFirst: Every upload starts with a free 10-second preview, signed in or not. Going on to the full song is a separate step that uses minutes.
items.outOfMinutes: Running out of minutes now opens a short dialog where you can buy a top-up in one click, instead of jumping to the pricing table.
items.playback: Fixed: clicking or seeking inside the score no longer stops playback.

v1_7.title: Printable scores, library search and new ways to see a song

items.pdf: Download any score as a printable PDF with the song title and credits, from Explore and from Your Library.
items.search: Explore has a full search page: filter, sort and page through every song in the library.
items.views: Song pages have two new views: Falling keys shows where your hands go on piano parts, and Spectrum overlays every stem's spectrogram.
items.phone: Upload phone recordings: M4A files from iPhone Voice Memos and most Android recorders now work, and so do OGG files.
items.codes: Got a signup code from a club or event? Its link adds free minutes to your account when you sign up.

v1_6.title: GrooveSheet in Chinese, with prices in yuan

items.geo: Visitors from mainland China now land on the Simplified Chinese site, and visitors from Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau on the Traditional Chinese site. Choose English and it stays English.
items.yuan: Visitors in mainland China see prices in yuan, the same on every plan card and in the comparison table.
items.scorePreviews: Explore cards show the first page of the real score, so you can see the notation before you open a song.
items.credits: Scores now carry the song title and a transcription credit on the page.
items.sync: Fixed: the score cursor and the drum audio now stay in step during playback.

v1_5.title: Drum transcription and a full-screen result view

items.drums: Drum transcription is here: choose Drums when you upload to get a drum score and MIDI, plus a drum kit view that lights up with every hit.
items.fullScreen: A finished piano transcription opens full screen, with the sheet music, piano roll and stems on one shared player.
items.refunds: If a transcription fails, the minutes it used go back to your account automatically.
items.noNotes: Fixed: a song with no piano in it now shows a clear "no notes found" message instead of breaking the viewer.
